issues.description: The solution repository's ray_sphere_intersect header declares a different function name than the implementation and callers. In solution_repository/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h the prototype is declared as intersect_ray_sphere(...), but the implementation (solution_repository/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp) and the caller in main.cpp use ray_sphere_intersect(...). This name/signature mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion when students compare template vs solution (the template header uses the correct name).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the function declaration in solution_repository/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h match the implementation and callers. Replace intersect_ray_sphere(...) with the prototype for ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius) (or alternatively rename the implementation and all callers to intersect_ray_sphere consistently). This restores a consistent public API and avoids compilation/link errors.

issues.description: The sphere-intersection function is referenced with two different identifiers across the template and solution artifacts: the template header and implementation declare/define ray_sphere_intersect(...), while the solution header declares intersect_ray_sphere(...) but the solution implementation still defines ray_sphere_intersect(...). This mismatch breaks the one-to-one mapping of the same conceptual entity (ray-sphere intersection routine) across artifacts, risks build/link confusion, and forces students to resolve an unintended naming difference rather than focusing on the algorithmic learning goal.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the function name consistent across header and implementation in all artifacts. Preferred quick fixes: (A) Change solution header declaration intersect_ray_sphere(...) to ray_sphere_intersect(...) to match the implementation and the template, or (B) rename the function definition in the solution .cpp to intersect_ray_sphere(...) and update all callers accordingly. Aligning the name removes accidental cognitive load and prevents build/link errors.
